full_judgment: Mr. Halder, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the bank has tried to assail that authenticity of the certificate mainly on two grounds; the first being that although the date of death was shown to be 10.03.1989, the certificate was issued after long 17 years on 15.11.2006. Secondly, although the address of late Habibur Rahman was shown to be at Dhaka, nevertheless, the certificate disclosed that he died at his own residence at Madaripur. Both the arguments advanced by Mr. Haider is fallacious. As to the issuance of the Death Certificate of late Habibur Rahman after long 17 years, in your view, the law does not impose any limitation with regard to issuance of Death Certificate. Simply because a Death Certificate was issued after 17 years of the death of a person, that by itself would not render the Death Certificate invalid. Secondly, with regard to fact that late Habibur Rahman was residing at Dhaka and died at Madaripur, we find the argument is absolutely fallacious in as much as a person may be residing temporarily in any place of Bangladesh, but ultimately he may die while residing at his own permanent residence, which may be in another city or district, as in the present case before us.
